provenance: rebuilt from the Money v2 demo (Claude's demo, not BIE output), 3 November 2026; drawn by code in draw.mjs; economy kit batch 3 (institutionBadge, paper, disc, vault, crowd, centralBank, committee, moneyBag) learned from 37 economy reference videos, 4 November 2026

sack.what: a tied grain sack, optionally labelled

clothStack.what: folded cloths stacked in four colours

saltPacket.what: a retail salt packet labelled नमक

note.what: one currency note; the colour follows the value

value.what: the printed value (2000/500/200/100/50/20/10 have their own colours)

coin.what: one coin in gold, silver or copper

calendar.what: a wall calendar with a heading

text.what: the heading (a month, a day count)

heap.what: a heap of salt or grain, dry or rain-wet

teaBrick.what: a pressed tea brick, optionally cracked

tobacco.what: tobacco leaves tied in a bunch

cheque.what: a bank cheque, optionally with an amount

accountCard.what: a titled account/summary card with an amount

bank.what: a bank building with columns, optionally labelled

qrStand.what: a counter QR-code stand (यहाँ scan करें)

phone.what: a phone showing home, scan, paid or received

mark.what: a judgement mark: tick, cross, question or circle

institutionBadge.what: a round badge naming an institution (central bank, bank, government, regulator, international body, cooperative, committee, market, company); BIE's stand-in for every logo or emblem

paper.what: a document: law, bond, licence, contract, bill or report, with title, year, amount, footer note and an optional rubber stamp

note.what: footer ribbon, e.g. the coupon or the term

disc.what: a coloured disc with a short word or number (RISK, 4%, FIXED) that can sit on and move between things

vault.what: a safe or vault holding note bundles: fill share, door open or closed, padlock, plate label and hanging tag (reserves kept aside, CRR, SLR, forex)

fill.what: 0..1 share of the shelves holding bundles

crowd.what: a crowd of small people in rows; a share from the left can be shaded and labelled, the rest coloured or dimmed (who is reached, who is left out)

centralBank.what: a central bank building (columns, a coin in the pediment, a vault door), with a name plate; no emblem

committee.what: a committee: generic members seated behind a table with a name plate (MPC, reform committees)

moneyBag.what: a tied money bag whose size carries the meaning (tiny to huge), optional label band

sign.what: symbol on the bag, empty for none

building.what: a generic building by kind: office, government (domed), exchange (ticker band), house, tower (real estate), shop, warehouse, village branch hut, court (columns, pediment, scales), factory (smoke; sick: a closed unit); optional name plate; no real landmark

sick.what: factory: a sick unit (no smoke, dim, broken window)

priceTag.what: a price tag; the old value can be struck and the new one written, with an up or down arrow

gauge.what: a semicircle meter (red, amber, green) with a needle at a value 0..1: rating, risk, index level, HDI

reverse.what: green on the left (low is good)

foreignNote.what: a generic foreign banknote with a currency sign ($, €, £, ¥ or ¤) and value; not a real design

barrier.what: a brick wall that blocks a path, optional label (a ban, a limit, a hurdle)

segmentedBar.what: one total drawn as a bar of labelled parts (shares); parts can be crossed, removed (the bar closes up) or glow: index baskets, CRR/SLR/loan split, budget heads, core vs headline

hide.what: part numbers removed; the bar closes up

shrink.what: the bar gets shorter when parts are hidden

cart.what: a hand cart (thela) on two wheels carrying vegetables, note bundles (a fund's pooled money) or goods, with a board

piggyBank.what: a piggy bank (savings, a small lender such as an NBFC), optional label on its side

ruler.what: a min-max ruler showing where a value sits between goalposts; a value outside is capped and turns red (HDI goalposts, normalised scores, legal ranges)

text.what: label over the pointer (default: the value)

hands.what: a giving hand and a receiving hand with notes, a coin or a paper between them, sides labelled (lending and borrowing, surplus to need, a payment)

coinJar.what: a glass jar of coins that fills to a level (savings, reserves, a fund growing or emptying)

pillars.what: pillars holding up a roof, each pillar labelled; one can crack or glow (the pillars of a framework, what holds a system up, what fails if one breaks)

n.what: number of pillars (0: one per label, else 3)

labels.what: pillar labels, left to right, separated by ;

briefcase.what: a briefcase with a name plate; open, it shows papers (a budget, a deal, a proposal carried in)

podium.what: a winners' podium of three blocks, 1st in the middle, 2nd left, 3rd right, each labelled (rankings, the largest three, top performers)

staircase.what: a staircase of labelled steps rising (or falling) left to right, one step can be outlined (stages, levels M0 to M4, a ladder of tiers, step-by-step growth)

n.what: number of steps (0: one per label, else 4)

labels.what: step labels, lowest first, separated by ;

desk.what: a desk with a front name plate and an optional chair behind (a lender's desk, an officer, a counter where someone sits)

chair.what: a chair: plain, office (on wheels) or big (a high seat of authority), optional label on the back

rope.what: a rope, rod or chain from left to right that ties two things together, with a sag, an angle and a label (a peg, a link, a fixed tie, a loose tie)

world.what: a whole place behind the lesson, wider than the stage for camera pans: market, bank hall, central bank, exchange floor, port, factory, village, office, court, city street, assembly hall, two countries across a border, a forex counter; and the places of a story whose state changes on the word: grain mandi (heaps = supply, buyers = demand, the board = price), food street, labour chowk, factory floor (N machines, k running), farm, river town, mohalla of graded homes, canteen, home, tea estate, bus stand, petrol pump, cinema or event venue, godown, island, two-sector farm and shed, dealing room, hospital, food shop or dhaba; place it at x 960, y 540, z 1 and stand people on its floor (y 885); its counts, levels, boards, shutters, weather and light change in its steps (was = the values just before, so boards strike the old value and things move); it is the place, not the thing being taught

label.what: the big sign of the place

signs.what: names on the numbered spots: stalls, counters, desks, sheds, shops, heaps, machines, plots, houses, menu rows, bays, pumps, cabins, ovens; the two countries' or two sectors' names; the forex board's rate rows; the exchange floor's ticker rows as name:price; a venue's price rows; separated by ;

count.what: stalls, counters, desks, containers, heaps, machines, plots, houses, menu rows, bays, pumps, cabins, ovens, huts (0: one per sign, else the kind default)

open.what: vault door open (bank hall, central bank)

crowd.what: faint people in the back (market, bank hall, exchange floor, city); for people who are counted use people

season.what: fields green or ready to harvest (village, farm, island, two-sector)

light.what: the time of day: a dawn chowk, an evening shift, a night street (windows and bulbs light up)

prices.what: board values separated by ; : one per stall, pump, bay, desk or menu row, or the place's one board (mandi price, chowk or estate wage, godown price); a food shop's whole rows (item and price)

was.what: the values just before this step, as key:value parts separated by | (prices:₹500|taken:2|shut:): a board strikes the old value beside the new; counts, levels, shutters, links and counters move from it over glide seconds; set was to '' on the next step

glide.what: seconds the things take to move from was after the step

people.what: counted people of the place: buyers (mandi, market), waiting workers (chowk), workers (factory floor, farm, tea estate), cooks, students, patients, the queue (bank hall), those turned away (venue); -1: the kind's usual number

taken.what: how many have moved to the place's other spot: hired onto the truck (chowk), in the shed (two-sector), seats filled (venue), beds filled (hospital), waiting at the till (food shop), sacks on the government truck (mandi); -1: the kind's usual

part.what: a second group in its own colour or place: of the filled seats the children or the bots (venue), idle workers on the bench (two-sector), dead fish (river town); -1: none

goods.what: how many things the place holds: sacks on the yard (mandi), harvest sacks (farm), the godown's stock (factory floor), trays (food shop), tiffins (home), live fish (river town), crates (island); -1: the kind's usual

level.what: the place's main level 0..1: the godown's fill, the crop's growth (farm), the river's dirt, the factory's emission, strain on the factory floor, smog (city), the vault's money (bank hall, island), the fridge (home), trust (dealing room); -1: the kind's usual

levels.what: a level 0..1 per numbered spot, separated by ; : a stall's unsold stock (market), a house's wealth from hut to bungalow (mohalla), a plot's share under the crop (farm), a tray's stock (canteen), a bus's load, the share of a stall's stools taken (food street)

counts.what: a count per numbered spot, separated by ; : the queue at each stall, cars at each pump or house, passengers at each bay, sacks in each heap, rotis by each cook; two-sector: food sacks;cloth rolls

shut.what: what is shut: numbered spots as 2,3 or all (stall shutters, covered carts, closed pumps, buses gone); 1 or its name for a one-door place (gate, door, road, shutter)

glow.what: what is in focus: numbered spots as 2,3 or names (fence, seats, oven, till, counter, stove, fridge, kitchen ...), separated by ,

running.what: how many of the machines run (factory floor); -1: all

seats.what: capacity: seats of the hall (venue), beds (hospital), stools per stall (food street); -1: the kind's usual

vehicles.what: carts arriving (mandi), contractors' trucks (chowk), cars on the road (city), fishing boats (river town); -1: the kind's usual

value.what: a counter's text: output (factory, factory floor), litres (petrol pump), drums tipped (river town), the till (food shop), revenue (bus stand), rent (godown), the index (exchange floor), the rate board (dealing room); a number rolls from its was value

notice.what: a second board or paper: the target or orders (factory floor), a government floor price and its truck (mandi), house full on the door (venue), the union office (tea estate), the day (canteen), the month (godown), the rent paper (food shop), a sale sign at the door (home), the legal limit on the chimney (factory)

weather.what: weather over an outdoor place; on a farm the crop wilts in a drought, insects swarm, water stands

crop.what: the crop of the fields (farm, island, two-sector); auto: the kind's own

item.what: what is made: the belt's and godown's thing and the machine's look (factory floor: shirt = sewing machines, cloth = looms), the food and its oven (food shop: roti = tandoor)

festive.what: festival lights strung over the place (market, food street, mohalla)

points.what: the index line's values separated by ; (exchange floor); with points: in was it draws itself after the step

links.what: lit loan lines between desks as pairs 1-2;2-3 (dealing room); they dim and break as level (trust) falls

neighbour.what: the neighbouring island across the water and its flag

on.what: the stove and the TV are on (home); false also darkens a venue's screen

rate.what: how fast the place works 0..1: the pipe's flow (river town), the belt (factory); -1: the kind's usual

flow.what: porters carry sacks in or out of the godown

filter.what: a filter on the chimney thins the smoke (factory, river town)

flow.what: a process world: places or people as nodes (houses, firms, government, banks, the central bank, the world) joined by arrows along which coins, notes or goods keep moving through the video; arrows labelled, lit one by one through steps (circular flow of income, credit creation, policy transmission, money leaving and returning)

nodes.what: label:kind;… kinds: office, government, exchange, house, tower, shop, warehouse, hut, court, bank, centralBank, people, globe, box (up to 8)

edges.what: from>to:label;… with 1-based node numbers, e.g. 1>2:wages;2>1:goods@goods (@coin|note|goods|dot: that arrow's token)

active.what: 1-based edges lit (others dashed), e.g. 1 then 1,2 in steps; empty: all

speed.what: trips per second along an arrow

bands.what: a zone scale: bands from good (green) to bad (red), each labelled with its range, a pointer at a value (types of inflation, safe and risky ranges, low to high)

value.what: a number for the pointer (empty: none)

text.what: pointer label (default: the value and unit)

fork.what: one lever, two directions: an arrow splits up and down, each branch with its label, its condition and its result (CRR less or more, rate cut or hike, what follows each way)

glow.what: the branch taken (the other greys out)

gapBars.what: two bars, what goes out against what comes in, the hatched gap between them named with its size (fiscal deficit, trade deficit, a savings or demand gap)

timeline.what: a timeline: events by year on an arrow (placed by their years when all are numbers), labels in two tiers, periods as coloured bands below; reveal events one by one (upto) and mark the one being told (at)

zones.what: from-to:label;… periods under the arrow, e.g. 1949-1991:govt

upto.what: show only the first n events (0: all)

even.what: equal spacing even when years are numbers

table.what: a table: column heads, row heads and cells (✓ and ✗ become tick and cross marks); rows can be revealed one by one (upto), a row or column glows (which parts make M1..M4, who does what, compare two systems)

cells.what: rows separated by |, cells by ; (✓ / ✗ for marks), e.g. ✓;✓;✗|✓;✗;✗

upto.what: show only the first n rows' contents (0: all)

fill.what: c:n;… column c shows only its first n cells (a step fills a column cell by cell on the voice: 4:1, then 4:2 …)

graph.what: the economics graph: axes with labels, up to six smooth or straight lines from data points (demand and supply, cost curves, indifference curves, budget lines, AD/AS, IS/LM, Phillips, Lorenz, J-curve), shaded areas (surplus, tax revenue, deadweight loss, profit), price floors and ceilings, shift arrows, shortage and surplus gaps, named axis points (P1, Q1), labelled dots that glide to a new equilibrium; built at the voice's speed: show reveals lines on a step, grow draws them over drawIn seconds after that step

dots.what: x,y:label;… e.g. 5,5:E; x,y<x0,y0:label glides from x0,y0 to x,y after the step that set it

drop.what: dashed lines from dots to the axes

drawIn.what: seconds the lines take to draw (0: at once)

show.what: 1-based lines shown ("1", then a step "1,2"); empty: all

grow.what: lines ("2") and areas ("a1") that draw over drawIn seconds after the step that set this; empty: every line draws from the start

bold.what: 1-based lines drawn thick (the one being talked about)

areas.what: label:x,y x,y x,y@#hex;… shaded polygons in data units (consumer surplus, tax revenue, deadweight loss)

hlines.what: y:label;… dashed horizontal lines (a price floor or ceiling)

vlines.what: x:label;… dashed vertical lines (a quota, a fixed supply)

arrows.what: x1,y1>x2,y2:label;… shift arrows in data units

gaps.what: x1,x2@y:label;… a bracket between two quantities at a price (shortage, surplus)

xTicks.what: x:label;… named points under the x axis (Q1, Q2)

yTicks.what: y:label;… named points left of the y axis (P1, P2)

glide.what: seconds a dot written x,y<x0,y0, a slide, a morph or an along point takes to move after the step

slide.what: k:dx,dy;… line k slides from dx,dy data units away into its place after the step (a shift seen happening)

morph.what: k:x,y x,y …;… line k reshapes from these points into its own after the step (a pivot, a new slope)

along.what: k@f:label;… a point on line k at fraction f of its points; k@f<k@f0 glides along the curve from f0; {x} {y} in the label read its values

segs.what: x1,y1>x2,y2:label;… dashed segments (a chord, a tangent, a reading line)

path.what: x,y:a;x,y:b;… a lettered adjustment path, points joined by arrows

pathUpto.what: how many points of the path are shown (a step reveals the next)

funnel.what: a funnel: much goes in at the wide top, a part comes out of the neck (reserve money into the multiplier, many inputs into one result); flip turns it so a little grows into much

roadmap.what: the lesson's road map: items in order, the current one framed, the ones done ticked (an agenda panel at the side that moves on as the lesson does)

done.what: items done so far (empty: those before at)

plant.what: a plant in a pot that grows from a seed to a tree (stage 0 to 1), coins or notes as its fruit (venture and seed funding, growth, compounding, an investment maturing)
